key_insight: A CNN trained on intracranial pressure cardiac cycles can use its attention maps to reveal waveform regions that correlate with patient body position, enabling interpretable feature discovery from physiological waveforms.
problem_solved: Addresses the lack of automated, interpretable methods for discovering meaningful features in intracranial pressure (ICP) monitoring waveforms and links waveform morphology to patient state (body position).
method: Collected ICP monitoring data from 60 patients and segmented recordings into individual cardiac cycles.
Trained a convolutional neural network to classify each cardiac cycle into one of seven body positions.
Extracted neural network attention maps to identify and localize regions of interest in the waveform for feature discovery and interpretability.
impact: Delivers a practical, explainable pipeline for physiologic time-series analysis that helps ML practitioners and clinicians discover clinically relevant waveform features and build more transparent models.
visual_elements: End-to-end pipeline diagram: data collection → cardiac-cycle segmentation → CNN classifier → attention extraction
Example ICP waveform annotated with attention heatmap showing highlighted regions across a cardiac cycle
Classification summary (e.g., confusion matrix or bar chart) across the seven body positions to convey model behavior
Schematic of cardiac-cycle segmentation and alignment across cycles to illustrate preprocessing
paper_title: A Framework for Feature Discovery in Intracranial Pressure Monitoring Data Using Neural Network Attention
paper_authors: Jonathan D. Socha, Seyed F. Maroufi, Dipankar Biswas, Richard Um, Aruna S. Rao
